### Create a Production Deployment with Vercel CLI

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/deployments

Run in your project's root directory to link your local directory to your Vercel Project and create a Production Deployment. A .vercel directory is added to store Project and Organization IDs.

```bash
vercel --prod
```

--------------------------------

### Link and deploy a Vercel project with vercel link and vercel deploy

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/cli/curl

Run these commands when no deployment URL is found for the project. You must be in a directory with a linked Vercel project that has at least one deployment.

```bash
# Link your project
vercel link

# Deploy your project
vercel deploy
```

--------------------------------

### deploy_to_vercel

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/deployments

Deploys a small, simple project from inline file contents when the Vercel CLI is unavailable and no usable remote git repository exists, or when the user explicitly requests an inline file deployment. Creation is asynchronous; poll get_deployment until READY, ERROR, or CANCELED before reporting the build outcome. This tool is available on root connections that expose deploy_to_vercel; project-scoped connections do not register it.

```APIDOC
## deploy_to_vercel

### Description
Deploy a small, simple project from inline file contents only when the Vercel CLI is unavailable and no usable remote git repository exists, or the user explicitly requests an inline file deployment. Prefer the Vercel CLI for local projects. If the intended source is pushed to a repository's production branch, use create_git_project. Do not reconstruct medium or large projects, binary assets, or dependency trees in tool arguments. This remote tool cannot read local paths or attachments. Files with actual contents are required. Limits: 300 files, 3 MiB per file, 4 MiB total encoded contents. Creation is asynchronous. Poll get_deployment until READY, ERROR, or CANCELED before reporting the build outcome.

### Parameters
- **target** (string) - Required - "preview" for a shareable non-production URL, or "production" to go live. Allowed values: "preview", "production".
- **name** (string) - Required - Project name. Vercel creates the project if it does not already exist.
- **files** (Array<object>) - Required - Required non-empty array of source files with their actual contents. A project name or local path alone cannot deploy. Do not include node_modules, .git, .env files, or secrets. Vercel installs dependencies and builds.
- **teamId** (string) - Optional - The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.
- **projectSettings** (object) - Optional - Optional build settings. Omit to let Vercel auto-detect the framework.
```

--------------------------------

### Deploy from a specific project directory with vercel --cwd

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploy

Use the --cwd flag to supply the path to the root directory of the Vercel project when running the vercel command.

```bash
vercel --cwd [path-to-project]
```

--------------------------------

### Override outputDirectory in vercel.ts

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-ts

Use the outputDirectory property in vercel.ts to override the Output Directory set in Project Settings for a deployment. In this example, the deployment looks for the build directory instead of the default public or . root directory.

```typescript
import type { VercelConfig } from '@vercel/config/v1';

export const config: VercelConfig = {
  outputDirectory: 'build',
};
```

--------------------------------

### Deploy Vercel project at a path with vercel [path-to-project]

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploying-from-cli

Deploys the Vercel project found at the provided path when it is a Vercel Project root. The first deployment of a new project is always a production deployment, even without --prod; later deployments without --prod create preview deployments.

```bash
vercel [path-to-project]
```

--------------------------------

### Override outputDirectory in vercel.json

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json

Use the outputDirectory property to override the Output Directory in Project Settings for a deployment. In this example, the deployment looks for the build directory instead of the default public or . root directory.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "outputDirectory": "build"
}
```
